literal: Dingyuan called on him and, facing his wife and daughters at a gathering, spoke in jest with slight impropriety.
idiomatic: Dingyuan called and, feasting with his wife and daughters, jested with slight impropriety.

literal: Xiu beat the drum, gathered the crowd, and was about to attack him; Dingyuan doffed his cap and bowed in apology and only after long time was he released.
idiomatic: Xiu beat the drum, gathered men to attack; Dingyuan doffed his cap and bowed long before he was released.

literal: Longzhi's younger brother Xingzhi, styled Zuyu.
idiomatic: Longzhi's younger brother Xingzhi, styled Zuyu.

literal: He was versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, plain and quiet.
idiomatic: He was versed in classics and conduct, plain and quiet.

literal: He held the posts of Inspector of Ying and Ji and Chief Steward of the Pacify-the-North Office.
idiomatic: He was Inspector of Ying and Ji and Chief Steward of the Pacify-the-North Office.

literal: In every post he held he had the reputation of a proper official.
idiomatic: Every post won him repute as a proper official.

literal: When he died, because of Longzhi's merit in aiding the founding, he was posthumously made Minister in the Palace and Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Wen.
idiomatic: At death, for Longzhi's founding merit, he was posthumously Palace Minister and Inspector of Yongzhou, posthumous title Wen.

literal: His son Xiaowan, styled Shiqian.
idiomatic: His son Xiaowan, styled Shiqian.

literal: Orphaned at seven, he was reared by Longzhi;
idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, Longzhi reared him;

literal: his love was very deep, and Longzhi petitioned to grant him his father's noble rank as Viscount of Fucheng.
idiomatic: his love was deep, and Longzhi petitioned to grant his father's rank Viscount of Fucheng.

literal: He held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.
idiomatic: He was Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.

literal: When he died he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Grand Storehouse.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Vice Minister of the Grand Storehouse.

literal: Xiaowan's nature was tranquil and he quite loved literary composition.
idiomatic: Xiaowan was tranquil and loved literary composition.

literal: Xing Shao, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and Wang Xin, Minister of the Seven Armies, were both advanced men of high talent; with Xiaowan the gap in years and rank was wide, yet meeting late they became deeply fond.
idiomatic: Xing Shao and Wang Xin, both eminent talents, met Xiaowan late in life despite wide gaps in age and rank, and friendship grew deep.

literal: When Xiaowan's coffin was to return home the two escorted him to the suburbs, weeping bitterly with grief that moved passers-by.
idiomatic: When Xiaowan's coffin went home both escorted him to the suburbs, weeping so bitterly passers-by were moved.

literal: Xiaowan's younger brother Xiaoyan, styled Shiguang, from youth cultivated himself; in learning he had bearing and elegance.
idiomatic: Younger brother Xiaoyan, styled Shiguang, cultivated himself from youth; in learning he had elegant bearing.

literal: He held the posts of Secretariat Assistant, Regular Attendant, and chief envoy on the mission to Chen; on the road he was remotely appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was Secretariat Assistant, Regular Attendant, and chief envoy to Chen; on the road he was remotely made Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

literal: On return he was punished for accepting Wei Shou's commission and issuing a warrant against his retainers' conduct on the journey; he was handed to the Southern Capital prison, sentenced to two hundred strokes of the whip, and struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: On return he was punished for taking Wei Shou's commission and issuing warrants against his retainers; the Southern Capital prison gave him two hundred lashes and struck his name away.

literal: Later he was made Director in the Joint Secretariat Ministry of Personnel and Friend to the Prince of Nanyang and went to Jinyang to handle secret affairs.
idiomatic: Later he was Joint Secretariat personnel director and Friend to the Prince of Nanyang and went to Jinyang for secret affairs.

literal: At He Shikai's mother's mourning all who had attached themselves went to wail.
idiomatic: At He Shikai's mother's mourning all hangers-on went to wail.

literal: The wealthy merchants Ding Zou and Yan Xing of Ye all performed filial mourning; one scholar too was within the mourners.
idiomatic: Ye merchants Ding Zou and Yan Xing all played filial mourners; one scholar too wailed among them.

literal: Xiaoyan entered to condole and, coming out, said to others: "South of Yan Xing and north of Ding Zou there is one court gentleman wailing exceedingly bitterly."
idiomatic: Xiaoyan condoled and, coming out, said, "South of Yan Xing, north of Ding Zou, one court gentleman wails exceedingly bitter."

literal: Those who heard passed it on.
idiomatic: Hearing men passed it on.

literal: Shikai learned of it and was greatly enraged.
idiomatic: Shikai learned and was greatly enraged.

literal: Later, when Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Gui reported that the Prince of Nanyang Chuo was arrogant and willful, Shikai therefore slandered him saying: "Xiaoyan followed Chuo outside, rode his spare horse, left the unit's ranks, and went apart in playful talk."
idiomatic: Later Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Gui reported Prince Chuo of Nanyang arrogant; Shikai slandered Xiaoyan for riding Chuo's spare horse, leaving ranks, and jesting apart.

literal: At that time Xiaoyan's daughter was consort to the Prince of Fanyang; for ritual reasons she therefore took leave to enter audience.
idiomatic: Then Xiaoyan's daughter was consort to the Prince of Fanyang; for ritual she took leave to enter audience.

literal: The Emperor thereupon had him beaten one hundred strokes with the horse whip and expelled; he also sent Gao Anagong to beat him again fifty strokes and he nearly died.
idiomatic: The Emperor had him horse-whipped one hundred strokes and expelled, and sent Gao Anagong for fifty more—he nearly died.

literal: Returning to Ye he went up and down in the Bureau for Collecting Writings.
idiomatic: Back in Ye he kept to the Collecting Writings Bureau.

literal: From this he sank into disuse.
idiomatic: From this he sank into disuse.

literal: After Shikai died he was made Unimpeded Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: After Shikai died he was Unimpeded Regular Attendant.

literal: Later, when peace was made with Zhou, he was made deputy chief envoy on the mission to Zhou.
idiomatic: Later, at peace with Zhou, he was deputy chief envoy to Zhou.

literal: When Zu Ting aided government he memorialized his entry into the Forest of Literature to compile the imperial overview.
idiomatic: When Zu Ting aided government he entered the Forest of Literature to compile the imperial overview.

literal: Xiaoyan's literary brush was not high, but he stood on elegant bearing, was skilled in witty talk, and his majesty was leisurely and refined; in bearing and in advance and retreat all men admired him.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan's brush was not high, yet he stood on elegant bearing, witty talk, leisurely majesty, and men admired his advance and retreat.

literal: Because Zu Ting liked to boast himself, he flattered him saying: "This is a minister in cap and gown, different from the rest."
idiomatic: Zu Ting boasted; Xiaoyan flattered him, "This is a minister in cap and gown, unlike the rest."

literal: Those close to the throne heard it and greatly resented it.
idiomatic: Court intimates heard and greatly resented it.

literal: Soon with his original office he also held the concurrent post of Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Soon he also held Right Assistant Minister with his original office.

literal: In his impeachments he mostly followed the ruler's intent.
idiomatic: His impeachments mostly followed the ruler's intent.

literal: At that time the monk Tanxian was favored by the Empress Dowager; rewards were thick and his carriage and dress exceeded measure.
idiomatic: The monk Tanxian was favored by the Empress Dowager; rewards were thick and dress exceeded measure.

literal: He also begged to be Patriarch over the Buddhist clergy; the later ruler's heart did not consent, but the Empress Dowager wished it and he therefore obtained the post.
idiomatic: He begged to be Patriarch over clergy; the later ruler refused but the Empress Dowager wished it and he obtained the post.

literal: Yet the later ruler often resented this.
idiomatic: Yet the later ruler often resented it.

literal: Because of another matter involving monks and nuns, a plaintiff's words implicated Tanxian; the ruler ordered the relevant office to investigate and impeach.
idiomatic: In another monks-and-nuns case a plaintiff implicated Tanxian; the ruler ordered investigation.

literal: Xiaoyan tried his case for taking bribes and brought him to extreme punishment; the rare treasures of his house were all confiscated for the state.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan tried his bribes and brought extreme punishment; rare treasures were confiscated.

literal: Thereupon he was formally appointed Left Assistant Minister and still reported on Gate affairs.
idiomatic: Thereupon he was formally Left Assistant Minister and still reported Gate affairs.

literal: His nature was quite haughty and he did not harmonize with the customs of the time; as favor rose higher he was all the more self-conceited; his movements were slow and he bowed to none—men of insight despised him.
idiomatic: He was haughty, ill-fit to custom, and as favor rose grew conceited; movements slow, bowing to none—men of insight despised him.

literal: He died with Cui Jishu and others for upright remonstrance.
idiomatic: He died with Cui Jishu and others for upright remonstrance.

literal: His sons Junque and Junjing were both moved to the northern border; the younger sons Junyan and Junzan were sent to the silkworm chamber.
idiomatic: Sons Junque and Junjing were moved north; younger sons Junyan and Junzan to the silkworm chamber.

literal: When Nan'an was defeated Junque and the two others were both punished with death.
idiomatic: When Nan'an fell Junque and the two others were executed.

literal: Xingzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye, from youth was clear in debate and had worldly usefulness.
idiomatic: Xingzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye, was clear in debate and useful in the world.

literal: Enfeoffed as Viscount of Tan, he was Inspector of Qingzhou and took many bribes.
idiomatic: Enfeoffed Viscount of Tan, he was Inspector of Qingzhou and took many bribes.

literal: Later he acted in Jinzhou affairs.
idiomatic: Later he acted in Jinzhou affairs.

literal: At the defeat at Shawei Yanzhi abandoned the province and fled north; because of Longzhi's relation he was spared death.
idiomatic: At Shawei's defeat Yanzhi abandoned the province and fled north; Longzhi's name spared his life.

literal: When he died he was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Duke of the Ministry of Works with the posthumous title Wengong.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Left Vice Minister and Duke of Works, posthumous title Wengong.

literal: His son Zuan inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited.

literal: Jian's eldest son Lin, styled Yanbao, held the post of Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
idiomatic: Jian's eldest son Lin, styled Yanbao, was Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

literal: With Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Nanping Feng Yan and others he deliberated on fixing the laws and orders; men of discernment praised it.
idiomatic: With Attendant Feng Yan of Nanping and others he fixed laws and orders; discerning men praised it.

literal: He served as Chief Steward to the Grand Marshal, Junior Minister under the Minister of the Masses, Inspector of Nanxia and Qing, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
idiomatic: He was Chief Steward to the Grand Marshal, Junior Minister under the Minister of the Masses, Inspector of Nanxia and Qing, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

literal: Lin's younger brother's son Su.
idiomatic: Lin's younger brother's son was Su.

literal: Su, styled Yuanyong, was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
idiomatic: Su, styled Yuanyong, was broadly versed in classics and histories.

literal: Grand Tutor Cui Guang saw him and prized him.
idiomatic: Grand Tutor Cui Guang saw and prized him.

literal: He held the post of Director in the Left Section for Army Affairs of the Ministry of War.
idiomatic: He was Director in the Left Section for Army Affairs.

literal: His nature was respectful and frugal; he did not make friends rashly—only with Cui Li and Li's cousin Hong was he especially close.
idiomatic: He was respectful and frugal, friendless save Cui Li and Li's cousin Hong.

literal: Most of the writings he composed are lost; a little more than ten scrolls remain.
idiomatic: Most writings are lost; a little over ten scrolls remain.

literal: Yi's cousin's son Kai, styled Siti, was Yi's grandson.
idiomatic: Yi's cousin's son Kai, styled Siti, was Yi's grandson.

literal: His father Quan was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.
idiomatic: His father Quan was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.

literal: Kai held the posts of Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: Kai was Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant.

literal: Later he entered the capital of Dai; his fame stood above Yi's son Xuanzhi.
idiomatic: Later he entered the Dai capital; his fame stood above Xuanzhi.

literal: Both were executed for the Sima affair.
idiomatic: Both were executed for the Sima affair.

literal: Kai's wife was the daughter of Lu Xuan.
idiomatic: Kai's wife was Lu Xuan's daughter.

literal: Kai's son Boda abandoned his mother and wife Lady Li and fled south of the river, changing marriage to the Fang clan.
idiomatic: Kai's son Boda abandoned mother and wife Lady Li, fled south of the river, and remarried into the Fang clan.

literal: At the end of Emperor Xianwen's reign Boda's son Xiujie entered within the passes.
idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xianwen Xiujie entered within the passes.

literal: Grandmother Lu was still alive, nearly a hundred years old.
idiomatic: Grandmother Lu still lived, nearly a hundred.

literal: Yet Lady Li had already died.
idiomatic: Lady Li was already dead.

literal: Xiujie held the post of Adviser to the Prince of Xianyang of Jizhou.
idiomatic: Xiujie was Adviser to the Prince of Xianyang of Jizhou.

literal: Returning to the clan, uncle Gui, styled Guangdu.
idiomatic: Of the clan, uncle Gui, styled Guangdu.

literal: He loved learning and thoroughly mastered the classics and their traditions.
idiomatic: He loved learning and mastered classics and traditions.

literal: With Grand Master of Splendid Virtue Sun Huiwei of Wuyi he shared purpose and were friendly.
idiomatic: With Grand Master Sun Huiwei of Wuyi he shared purpose and friendship.

literal: Huiwei often pushed Gui saying: "In classical meaning Feng Sheng surpasses me in more matters than I can count."
idiomatic: Huiwei often said, "In classical meaning Feng Sheng surpasses me in more than I can count."

literal: He quite cultivated himself in purity; his bearing was very grand.
idiomatic: He cultivated purity; his bearing was grand.

literal: Some said: "Scholars do not trouble with adornment—why is this worthy alone thus?"
idiomatic: Some said, "Scholars do not dress up—why is this worthy alone so?"

literal: Gui heard it and laughed: "The gentleman sets his cap and robes in order and honors what men see—why must one be unkempt and filthy before he is worthy?"
idiomatic: Gui laughed, "The gentleman orders cap and robes and honors what men see—must one be filthy to be worthy?"

literal: The speaker flushed and withdrew.
idiomatic: The speaker flushed and withdrew.

literal: As Concurrent Regular Attendant he bore credentials to Goguryeo.
idiomatic: As Concurrent Regular Attendant he bore credentials to Goguryeo.

literal: King Yun of Goguryeo relied on his remote distance and claimed illness and would not personally receive the edict in audience.
idiomatic: King Yun relied on distance, claimed illness, and would not receive the edict in person.

literal: Gui sternly questioned him and instructed him in the great meaning; Yun then turned north and received the decree.
idiomatic: Gui sternly questioned him and taught the great meaning; Yun turned north and received the decree.

literal: When the mission returned he was transferred to Director in the Ministry for Evaluating Merit and made Rectifier of his native commandery.
idiomatic: On return he was Director for Evaluating Merit and Rectifier of his commandery.

literal: Cui Xiu of Bohai entered office as Director in the Ministry of Personnel; because of his elder brother he handled Gui's evaluation.
idiomatic: Cui Xiu of Bohai became personnel director and, for his elder brother, handled Gui's evaluation.

literal: Gui said: "Law is the business of the realm—it cannot be bent because of an old patron."
idiomatic: Gui said, "Law is the realm's business—it cannot bend for an old patron."

literal: Xiu sighed at his upholding what was right.
idiomatic: Xiu sighed at his rectitude.

literal: In the central offices Gui was called refined and Confucian.
idiomatic: In central offices Gui was called refined and Confucian.

literal: He was made Erudite of the National University, acting Unimpeded Regular Attendant, and sent to comfort the mountain Hu of Fenzhou.
idiomatic: He was National University Erudite, acting Unimpeded Regular Attendant, comforting Fenzhou mountain Hu.

literal: The Prince of Qinghe, Minister of Works, Yi, memorialized to repair the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy; an edict ordered the hundred offices to assemble in deliberation.
idiomatic: Prince Yi of Qinghe, Minister of Works, memorialized to repair Bright Hall and Imperial Academy; the hundred offices were ordered to deliberate.

literal: Gui argued:
idiomatic: Gui argued:

literal: The "Artificer" office in the Offices of Zhou says: the Hall of the Xia had the World Room, the Yin the Double Roof, the Zhou the Bright Hall—five chambers, nine steps, four doors, eight windows.
idiomatic: The Zhou Offices Artificer says: Xia's World Room, Yin's Double Roof, Zhou's Bright Hall—five chambers, nine steps, four doors, eight windows.

literal: Zheng Xuan says: "Sometimes ancestral temple is named, sometimes royal sleeping quarters, sometimes Bright Hall—interlocking words to show one system."
idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says, "Sometimes temple, sometimes royal chambers, sometimes Bright Hall—interlocking words for one system."

literal: Thus the Bright Halls of the Three Dynasties were one in system.
idiomatic: Thus the Three Dynasties' Bright Halls shared one system.

literal: Considering Zhou with Xia and Yin, additions and subtractions differ.
idiomatic: Zhou against Xia and Yin differs in additions and subtractions.

literal: As for the Bright Hall, they followed without change; clearly the meaning of five chambers obtained Heaven's number.
idiomatic: Yet the Bright Hall they followed unchanged—five chambers obtain Heaven's number.

literal: Therefore Zheng Xuan also says: "Five chambers image the Five Phases."
idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also says, "Five chambers image the Five Phases."

literal: Then nine steps image the Nine Regions; four doors reach the four seasons; eight windows penetrate the eight winds—truly an unchanging great model and the constant pattern of a state.
idiomatic: Nine steps image the Nine Regions; four doors the four seasons; eight windows the eight winds—an unchanging great model and a state's constant pattern.

literal: If above round and below square to model Heaven and Earth, a water channel encircling the palace to regulate viewers, thatched cover and white hangings for substance and ornament, red tassels and white tassels for doors and windows—all are what the classics record and the clear meaning of institution.
idiomatic: Round above, square below to model Heaven and Earth; water channel encircling the palace; thatched cover and white hangings; red and white tassels for doors and windows—all are what classics record and institution's clear meaning.
